text:
Sam K: Hey team — quick question on benefits + payroll. I started on Mon (UK-based) and want to confirm: 1) is health insurance effective date the next month or retro to my start? 2) PTO accrual pro‑rata? 3) my first pay deposit seems delayed for international bank — who should I ping? I uploaded visa docs as `visa_i94.pdf` to the portal. @Maya (People Ops) any tips? Thanks!

Maya (People Ops): Welcome, Sam! Congrats and great q's. Quick answers: health coverage is normally effective the 1st of the month after 30 days, PTO accrues pro‑rata monthly. For international bank issues ping payroll — @Ben - Payroll — and DM me your start date so I can check if we can make an exception for an earlier effective date. Also double check you uploaded passport + I-94 (we need both).

Ben - Payroll: Hey Sam — welcome. If the portal shows a failure it's usually due to missing routing details (ABA vs IBAN/BIC). Can you screenshot the error? If your bank uses IBAN only, include the full IBAN + BIC. If it's urgent we can do an off‑cycle pay — fill the off‑cycle form: https://redwood.pay/forms/off-cycle and mark it URGENT. If you need cash immediately, submit an expense with tag `newhire-advance` and cc payroll.

Alex (Benefits): Hi Sam — you were auto-enrolled into Redwood Core PPO by default. If you want HSA instead, elect within 30 days; HSA contributions start the first payroll after election. Note: HSA tax treatment depends on your country of residence — since you're UK-based we may need Legal review.

Sam K: Thanks. The payroll portal shows: "Deposit failed: invalid ABA" and my bank only provided IBAN/BIC (no ABA). Also I named the upload `SamK_visa.zip` — the portal accepted it but wanted separate passport + I-94 files.

Ben - Payroll: Got it. Send me a DM with the screenshot and last 4 of your sort code. For USD payroll to UK accounts we sometimes route via a US intermediate bank; if the ABA is required you'll need to provide an alternate receiving bank. I've started an off‑cycle payment request for you — can take up to 48 hours. Meanwhile, submit the travel/relocation receipt on Expensify with policy `relocation` if you need reimbursement faster.

Maya (People Ops): On holidays — we apply the country of residence policy by default. UK public holidays will be pro‑rated based on calendar days in your first month. Example: start Mar 10 → you get monthly accrual * (remaining_days/total_days). I'll update your country on the benefits profile now.

Sam K: Confirming UK policy please. Also I just uploaded separate files `SamK_passport.pdf` and `SamK_I94.pdf` to the onboarding portal — should be visible.

Alex (Benefits): Perfect. Reminder: you have 30 days from your start date to change benefit elections; otherwise you wait until open enrollment. If you need to submit a moving or one‑time reimbursement (e.g., boxes, flight), put it in Expensify under `relocation` and tag `people-ops` so we spot it quickly.

Maya (People Ops): I updated your residence and flagged your case in Workday — benefits team will confirm effective dates there and we'll send you the exact accrual numbers by EOD. @Ben - Payroll any update on the deposit?

Ben - Payroll: Checked with the bank — they rejected because the IBAN needed a country prefix in our field. I manually kicked an off‑cycle conversion to a temporary US account and scheduled payment. Expect funds within ~48 hours. I'll DM instructions to update your bank details properly (IBAN/BIC fields). :thumbsup:

Sam K: Amazing, thank you all. One last small thing — do I need to fill extra tax forms for UK? I saw a W-4 in the onboarding checklist but not sure if it applies.

Maya (People Ops): For UK residents we use local tax guidance. We sent a short checklist by email (P45/P60 guidance and residency forms). I'll re-send it to you and loop Legal if there are cross‑border items. Ping me if you don't get the email in the next hour.

Ben - Payroll: Followed up in DM with the exact field names to change. If anything still fails after that we'll process a manual correction in payroll and confirm via email.

Sam K: Thanks, all — appreciate the quick responses.
